paras: In the 1905 Rockport, Kentucky, clash, fifteen to twenty armed white men fired on a crowd of Black people at Rockport, Ohio County, on Sunday, August 13, 1905. No one was reported seriously hurt; fifteen white men and four Black men were charged.
On Saturday night a street row between a Black man and a white man, which the Hartford Republican traced to a dispute over "perhaps five cents worth of cheese," ended in an exchange of revolver fire.

The Hartford Herald said about thirty Black men "had congregated out side of town and defied arrest," and armed white men went out to arrest them. The Republican said instead that the whites heard armed Black men were coming to town, "did not wait," found a crowd at Pet Render's, opened fire, and "put them to flight." The sheriff, asked by the police judge to come, said he would do so only with a writ.

On Monday a Black man named Render had a writ issued at Hartford for fifteen white men, charging them with banding together to disturb or injure others. County Attorney W. H. Barnes sent the case to the Rockport Police Court for an examining trial. The Herald also reported, as hearsay, a rope and note left Monday night ordering a Black man to leave or be hanged. A week later it reported that Dee Render, Pet Render, John Render and John Short, "all of color," had been arrested and would be tried with the white men; no report of the outcome appears.

Only Hartford's two papers carried the episode. The Herald, under "Almost Race War," cast the white men as an arresting party and called some of them "the best citizens of Rockport." The Republican's "Clash at Rockport" stated that the whites opened fire, while calling the crowd "dark skins." Neither paper named the white men charged, though the Herald named the arrested Black men.
The papers differ on why the whites went out, to arrest men who had defied arrest (Herald) or to meet a reported armed party (Republican); both versions came from the white side.

reader.title: 1905 Rockport, Kentucky, clash
bases: Fifteen to twenty armed white men, acting without an officer or writ, fired on a crowd of Black people at Pet Render's and drove them off, with no one reported seriously hurt (A1, A2).

Two separate Hartford papers independently report the Saturday fight, the Sunday shooting by armed whites, and the writ for fifteen white men, with differing details (A1, A2), and a later Herald item reports the resulting arrests (A3).

accounts.label: Hartford Herald (local, white side)
accounts.gist: About thirty Black men gathered outside town Sunday and 'defied arrest'; several white men armed themselves and went out to arrest them; shots were fired, no one seriously injured.

accounts.label: Hartford Republican (local)
accounts.gist: On a report that armed Black men were coming to town, fifteen or twenty armed whites went out without waiting, found a crowd at Pet Render's, opened fire and put them to flight.

accounts.label: Black complainant (via affidavit)
accounts.gist: A Black man named Render swore out a writ charging fifteen white men; his own account is not printed.

framing.detail: The Herald headlined 'Almost Race War', presented the white men as an arresting party, called some of the accused 'the best citizens of Rockport', doubted the writ, and repeated a hearsay boast by the threatened Black man.
The Republican headlined 'Clash at Rockport', called the cause 'a trivial matter' and said the whites did not wait and opened fire, while calling the Black crowd 'dark skins'.
The Herald's follow-up named the four arrested Black men 'all of color' and noted the white men would be tried at the same time, without naming them.
